content.comment_body: While editing a project, I encountered a persistent Java error when trying to delete an instruction, which caused repeated popups with every click on the circuit diagram. After saving, restarting [product_name] and reloading, the project now won’t load—the progress bar reaches 100% and then nothing happens. Rebooting the computer didn’t resolve it, though other projects can be opened without issues. Is there a way to repair this project? Losing work on a mature project would be disastrous. I’m running the latest version of [product_name] ([version_no]).
Can you try uploading the program? Opening it elsewhere may help determine whether the issue lies in the program file or with the software itself.
I think uploading isn’t possible unless the file can be opened first, so unfortunately no.
Could you upload your program file here for review?
Sure, here is the problematic file.
The file appears to be really corrupted. It doesn’t open; the progress bar cycles to 100% and then restarts repeatedly.

Hello everyone. The issue seems to stem from the software and the ladder format. [user_name] — your program does open with [product_name] ([version_no]). I’ve attached two versions: the original ladder format file, saved again, and a copy converted to FBD format. You should be able to open the FBD file with the newer version of the software.
Thank you! Now I know how to resolve this problem in the future if important projects become affected.

I’ve faced a similar issue. I could open the file on another computer with [product_name] ([version_no]), but saving it and transferring it to the newer version causes the same problem. Saving both lld and lsc formats didn’t help—the new version won’t open either file. Is there any action needed in [product_name] ([version_no]) to make the file compatible with the latest software? As usual, I’m in a time crunch! Thanks.
Please upload your program to the forum for troubleshooting.
It’s proprietary and I’m concerned about job security. Is there a safe recommendation you can offer?
You can send me a private message and attach the file. I can help convert it from [version_no] lld to [version_no] lld.

I’m experiencing the same issue, but I used FBD in [product_name] ([version_no]) rather than ladder format. Would exporting to [product_name] ([version_no]) help? If so, where can I find a demo version of [product_name] ([version_no])?
A demo version of [product_name] ([version_no]) is no longer available on [company_name]'s website. What exactly is your issue? Maybe I can assist you.

I have the same problem as the original poster. My file, shown in the attachment, will not open at all and triggers an error box. However, mine is a .lsc file whereas theirs was .lld, and [user_name] solved it by converting the .lld to .lsc using [product_name] ([version_no]). I’m also curious about what might be causing this issue.
Can you upload your program to the forum? Which model are you using?
If privacy is a concern, maybe they could send the file via private message. I’m sure you’d keep it confidential. Thanks a lot.
Hi [user_name], do you think importing the project to [version_no] would resolve the problem? I’m currently working with [version_no].
I’ve sent you a private message.
I couldn’t open the file, either. The progress bar stops at 99% and then nothing happens. Importing in project mode returns the error described previously.
Do you still have [product_name] ([version_no]) installed on your computer?

The poster informed me that it’s an [version_no] file. Attempting to open it with older versions such as [version_no] gives an error: 'Failed to load the file.' This usually means it was created with a more recent software version.
Strange—did you receive the original program file or the one that was converted?
I provided him with the original program.

From previous experience: In LLD programming, a function block like ON-delay involves two blocks—a block with parameters and a coil for the result. Usually, these are paired next to each other, but sometimes split across lines. If you copy, paste, or delete without selecting both blocks, it may corrupt the program. I recommend using FBD instead of LLD. If a project becomes corrupted, [product_name] ([version_no]) might temporarily repair it, but this is only a short-term solution in my experience.
A new question from [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread with the subject 'Corrupt [product_name] file.' Best regards, [user_name]

Hi, I’ve recently encountered this problem as well. A file created in [product_name] ([version_no]) refuses to open—the progress bar stays at 100% with no error message. I don’t want to lose a day of work. Is there any solution? Thanks to everyone for the assistance.
No solution at the moment; please submit a support request.
I can’t open this either! I have the same issue. Please assist :(
Submit a support request. As a side note: programming in FBD format can help avoid these issues.
A new question from [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled 'Can someone help me with a corrupt project file please?' Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users have encountered major file corruption issues with [product_name] ([version_no]), especially when working with ladder diagrams. A Java error during instruction deletion led to the software freezing while loading affected projects, with the progress bar either looping or getting stuck. Other projects can still be opened, and some files are accessible through older versions or format conversion, suggesting compatibility or software bugs centered on ladder diagrams. There is notable concern over loss of work and difficulties in recovering projects.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] ([version_no]) to reliably save and manage projects without risk of data corruption, ensure compatibility for ladder diagram formats, and offer effective recovery options for affected files. They seek robust project integrity solutions to prevent loss of critical or time-consuming work.
